Skills for Industry Competitiveness and Innovation Program (SICIP)

QA visit: steps for the visiting team

Order of work on the day
Use with the QA Visit Report (Annex-3, sections 1–15)
Notice to centreAnnounced. Date agreed and document list sent in advance.
Time on siteOne full working day; two days for a large centre
What it checksAll 9 quality components, from registration to certification and job placement
RecordQA Visit Report (Annex-3), signed by every visiting officer

Preparation in the office (one to two weeks before)

#TaskWhat to doReport
P1Agree the dateFix the date(s) with the Principal / Centre Manager on a day when batches are running. Ask that the Principal, trainers, job placement officer and accounts person be present.1
P2Send the document listSend "QA visit: documents to keep ready at the institute" so every file is in one place, sorted by course and batch.2–10
P3Study the centreRead the MoU and Business Plan, the PIU / SDCMU capacity assessment, the last QA report and all surprise visit reports since. Take target, enrolled, certified, job-placed and dropout figures from TMS.1.20–1.60
P4Split the workAssign report sections to team members, for example one officer on finance and records (2–5), one on training and assessment (6–10). Pick 3 trainees from TMS to trace end to end in step 5.—

Order of work at the centre

#WhenStepWhat to doReport
1Start, 20–30 minOpening meetingExplain the purpose, the agenda and who checks what. Record the people met, registration status and MoU details, and confirm the course table and cumulative figures against TMS.1.00–1.50
2Morning, while classes runWalk the training floor
  • Count trainees in each running batch and compare with the register and TMS; ask the reasons for dropouts.
  • Observe at least one class and one workshop: delivery method, tools against the CS list, consumables, PPE in use, utilities, ventilation, lighting and fire safety.
1.60–1.62, 8, 9
3MorningHear trainees and trainersTalk to at least two trainees with no staff present, then to the trainers on the training environment and resources. Record each person's feedback.11, 12
4Midday to afternoonReview documents by componentGo through sections 2 to 10 in order, with the responsible staff member present for each. For every criterion, see the evidence itself, not a verbal answer, and mark it seen, not seen or not applicable.2–10
5AfternoonTrace 3 traineesFollow each trainee picked in P4 through advertisement, application, admission form, attendance, formative and final assessment, certificate and job placement record. A broken link shows where the system fails.4, 5, 10
6AfternoonCheck earlier findingsOpen the monitoring logbook and check the action taken on each finding of the last QA and surprise visits.2, 8
7Before exit, 30 minTeam discussionWithout centre staff, agree the strengths and weaknesses of each of the 9 components, the major findings and the recommendations.13–15
8End, 20–30 minExit meetingPresent the major findings and recommendations to the Principal and staff. Agree an action and a date for each recommendation, and ask the centre to enter them in the monitoring logbook.14, 15

Rules on site

  • See the training floor in the morning while trainees are present; read files after classes end.
  • Accept only documents shown to you. "It is in the office" is recorded as not seen.
  • Sample and cross-check: TMS against registers, registers against vouchers, placement register against employer letters.
  • Photograph evidence that supports a weakness or a major finding.
  • Keep the discussion of ratings and findings inside the team until the exit meeting.

After the visit

  • Complete every section of Annex-3 and have every visiting officer sign it.
  • Submit the report to your supervisor and file it with the centre's visit records.
  • Send the recommendations and agreed dates to the centre in writing.
  • Report any serious non-compliance (ghost trainees, fees charged, false placements) to your supervisor at once.
  • Use the recommendations as the issue list for the next surprise or QA visit.
TMS = Training Management System, MoU = memorandum of understanding, PIU = project implementation unit, SDCMU = skills development coordination and monitoring unit, CS = competency standard, PPE = personal protective equipment. Section numbers refer to Annex-3.
